claims.text: MOA: beta-lactam; binds and inactivates enzymes required for bact cell wall synth.
claims.quote: All beta-lactams bind to and inactivate enzymes required for bacterial cell wall synthesis.

claims.text: Treats: extremely broad: gram (-) bacilli, anaerobes, most Enterobacterales (incl AmpC/ESBL producers), MSSA and strep.
claims.quote: Carbapenems are parenteral bactericidal beta-lactam antibiotics that have an extremely broad spectrum. They are active against Gram-negative bacilli Anaerobes Most Enterobacterales (including those that produce AmpC beta-lactamase and extended-spectrum beta-lactamase [ESBL], although Proteus mirabilis tends to have a higher imipenem minimum inhibitory concentration [MIC]) Methicillin-sensitive staphylococci and streptococci, including Streptococcus pneumoniae (except possibly strains with reduced penicillin sensitivity)

claims.text: Treats (gaps): ertapenem misses E. faecalis and P. aeruginosa (imipenem/meropenem cover many); E. faecium, Stenotrophomonas and MRSA are resistant to all.
claims.quote: Most Enterococcus faecalis and many Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains, including those resistant to broad-spectrum penicillins and cephalosporins, are susceptible to imipenem and meropenem but are resistant to ertapenem. However, meropenem is less active against E. faecalis than imipenem. Carbapenems are active synergistically with aminoglycosides against P. aeruginosa. However, E. faecium, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, and methicillin-resistant staphylococci are resistant.

claims.text: Parenteral bactericidal beta-lactams w an extremely broad spectrum.
claims.quote: Carbapenems are parenteral bactericidal beta-lactam antibiotics that have an extremely broad spectrum.

claims.text: Seizures and other CNS effects (meropenem label), mostly w CNS disorders, meningitis or renal impairment
claims.quote: Seizures and other adverse CNS experiences have been reported during treatment with Meropenem for injection. These experiences have occurred most commonly in patients with CNS disorders (e.g., brain lesions or history of seizures) or with bacterial meningitis and/or compromised renal function
imipenem is not used in meningitis because it may cause seizures.
Clostridioides difficile- associated diarrhea (ranging from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis) has been reported.

claims.text: Hypersensitivity to carbapenems or prior anaphylaxis to beta-lactams.
claims.quote: Meropenem for injection is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any component of this product or to other drugs in the same class or in patients who have demonstrated anaphylactic reactions to beta (β)-lactams.

claims.text: Preg: only when safer abx aren't an option.
claims.quote: Carbapenems should only be used in pregnant patients when safer antibiotics are not an option.
claims.locator: Use of Carbapenems During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Lowers valproic acid levels (meropenem label): risk of breakthrough seizures.
claims.quote: Co-administration of meropenem for injection with valproic acid or divalproex sodium reduces the serum concentration of valproic acid potentially increasing the risk of breakthrough seizures.
